title: Palace theatre drummers and Wilbert Hogan
summary: Andrew Jackson at the Palace, drummers Earl Palmer, Weedy Morris and Ed Blackwell, and praise for Wilbert Hogan who took his place with Hampton.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: All these guys. He was a drummer at the palace? He was a drummer at the palace.

He was a drummer at the palace. He was a drummer at the palace and at the rich. He said right in the front seat, as close as you and I, you know, he'd be playing. Then he used to tell me, he said, you can't do this, you know. But he was a man and I was a child. I said, I'm going to practice that, you know, not go home. We didn't have a practice pad. We made our own little practice pads. And all of this, you know, learning and being around these fellas. And then later on, through the years, he'd meet guys like Earl Palmer, Weedy Morris, and that's Edris Muhammad's brother. Yeah. Are you aware of Weedy? Yeah, I know. Yeah, I know. Okay, he died in St. Louis. You know, Chenu, Cornise, Coleman, Ed Blackwell. And one gentleman I hope somebody says something about is Wilbert Hogan. You know, nobody says anything about Wilbert Hogan. He was the first brother that I know from here to graduate from Juilliard School of Music. He went to Book of Washington. But he was a hell of a drummer. He died a few years ago. He played with everybody with different shows. As a matter of fact, when I came back from Lionel Hampton, we were in New York, 50, late, 56, 57. He'd take my place with Hampton.
Did he go with Hampton? Yeah.

Because I said, man, you want to die? No, I don't want to deal with Hampton. We were in New York. And I came home. And the next thing I knew I got a word that Wilbert was playing with him. But he played with everybody. And he was a very dear friend. But nobody mentions his name, I hope. Remember that name, New Orleans.
